summary: The complete diff preserves original byte spans for retained Squeeze input without changing rune comparison or pattern selection. No counterexample was found in an independent 1,800,495-case input/pattern sweep; existing Squeeze tests also pass.
evidence: Read runs/2026-10-15/claim.md, the complete git diff 96b69c7949060424ce4778947e3e32112cb7e3d5 ac5ce55dcb3810dc8a5d2a1cd22219e0ef972756, Squeeze and Translator implementation, allocBuffer, stringBuilder definitions, the test assertion helper, CONTRIBUTING.md, go.mod and .github/workflows/go.yml. No dated report, run-level result.json, other review, or author reasoning was used.

The only production changes replace two output.WriteRune(r) calls with output.WriteString(str[:size]). utf8.DecodeRuneInString, last/skipSqueeze updates, pattern lookup, buffer initialization, and deletion branches are unchanged. For valid UTF-8 these writes are equivalent. For an invalid decoded byte, the new write copies that original byte instead of encoding U+FFFD. The loop calls DecodeRuneInString only on a nonempty suffix, so the consumed byte slice is in bounds.

All pre-existing test inputs, expected outputs, and the equality assertion are unchanged. Eleven Squeeze cases were added, including retained malformed bytes, nonmatching patterns, Unicode, NUL and literal U+FFFD. git diff --check 96b69c7949060424ce4778947e3e32112cb7e3d5 ac5ce55dcb3810dc8a5d2a1cd22219e0ef972756 passed.

There is no signature, exported type, dependency, module-path, or go directive change. WriteString and ordinary byte slicing were already used in the baseline, including allocBuffer and Translator.Translate, so the patch introduces no language/API requirement beyond the declared Go 1.12 minimum. Runtime compatibility testing in this review used Go 1.26.9 linux/arm64, not Go 1.12.

Created a separate HTTPS clone of https://github.com/huandu/xstrings.git, fetched the exact candidate from the primary local checkout, and checked out a new criterion-candidate branch. HEAD was ac5ce55dcb3810dc8a5d2a1cd22219e0ef972756 and its parent was 96b69c7949060424ce4778947e3e32112cb7e3d5. No tracked candidate source was modified; only the independent criterion_test.go was added to that disposable clone.

Independent checker: runs/2026-10-15/reviews/criterion_test.go. It constructs byte spans from Go range offsets and uses direct pattern predicates, without reusing Squeeze's state machine or Translator. It checks every zero-, one-, and two-byte string plus all sequences of up to four selected ASCII, Unicode, invalid-byte and truncated-encoding tokens. Fifteen patterns cover all-runes, selected literals, nonmatches, inversion, ascending and descending ranges, NUL, literal U+FFFD, invalid pattern bytes, Unicode ranges and escaped punctuation.

Executed python3 night.py run --checkout .work/checkouts/huandu-xstrings-review-criterion-20261015 --image golang:1.26-bookworm --timeout 240 -- sh -c with the exact script recorded in runs/2026-10-15/reviews/criterion-check.json: export GOCACHE=/work/.gocache GOPATH=/work/.gopath GOTMPDIR=/work/.gotmp; mkdir -p "$GOTMPDIR"; go version; go test -count=1 -run "^Test(CriterionSqueezeBytePreservation|Squeeze)$" -v ./...; test -z "$(gofmt -l criterion_test.go)". The command passed with exit code 0 using image sha256:d9c68c2c51161e12fd77e4c6320687c9cd86e1af1e3ad6e6cd63ff970641453c and source snapshot sha256 7c86ccbe09b608a1b60896bc509fe60f846dc0b911beaaf2fd00a926980febba.

Unmodified helper records and logs are saved as runs/2026-10-15/reviews/criterion-check.json and criterion-check.log. The log reports 1,800,495 input/pattern pairs passing the byte-span oracle and TestSqueeze passing. The checker's formatting check also passed.

The initial helper invocation used sh -lc and exited 127 before executing any Go code because that shell could not find Go. Its unmodified record and log are preserved as runs/2026-10-15/reviews/criterion-setup-failure.json and criterion-setup-failure.log. Retrying with sh -c on the identical source snapshot and image passed. This was a check-launch issue, not a candidate defect.
confirmed_scope: Squeeze preserves the original bytes of each decoded input segment it retains, including invalid UTF-8 after buffer initialization and when a pattern selects no input. The patch leaves adjacency comparisons and pattern selection unchanged: adjacent malformed bytes and literal U+FFFD may still compare as the same RuneError and be squeezed when selected. Valid UTF-8 output is unchanged by the two write substitutions. The finite boundary sweep and code review support this localized correction; no performance improvement or universal correctness of Squeeze or its pattern parser is claimed.
